boundary_decision.interaction: None. The term is defined inside the Run Context and crosses no boundary.

domain_forces: Run is used in every architecture decision, specification, handbook and package comment in this repository and is defined in none of them.

The previous record defined Run as 'Skill trial lifecycle.' and cited a line of the DDD convergence table that only enumerates the commands the Run aggregate accepts, so the definition rested on evidence that did not carry it.
implementation_design.decision: Define Run in the Context Map, the document that already says what each Bounded Context is, and cite that line.
rejected_alternatives: Promote the old definition: its cited line enumerates commands and does not define the term.
Define Run as one execution: run_attempts is unique on (run_id, attempt_number), so an attempt is the execution and the Run is the retryable unit.
Say the result is evaluated: running transitions directly to failed, cancelled or timed_out, so not every Run reaches evaluating.

Define it in the architecture decision that owns Run orchestration: this repository reserves decision numbers and filenames for those documents and their index, so a Registry citation to one is refused by the adr-citations gate.

record.name: Run
record.definition: One requested trial of a single Skill Version against a single frozen Test Case snapshot, within a Workspace, carried out through one or more attempts on a sandbox Provider, and ending in a single terminal status. An attempt is the execution; the Run is the retryable unit whose identity a reassignment does not change.

approvals.scope: The definition of Run, derived from the runs and run_attempts schema and the Run state machine, as written into the Context Map
